findings.title: Resolve the Agent Observability project
findings.gap: The deployment has no resolved Agent Observability project resource or project identifier.
findings.impact: Agent traces have no verified project destination.
findings.product_outcome: An existing or authorized newly created project resource is available as the trace destination.
findings.required_fix: Resolve an existing project resource and its identifier, or create one through the configured supported Agent Observability SDK/API endpoint when authorized; never invent an identifier. A compatible local gateway delegates the normal resource request using its active Studio cloud connection, without an application cloud token. Preserve an optional operator project name or ID, verify an ID without creating a replacement, and use a stable service-derived name when none is supplied. Reuse an exact existing project; attempt creation of a selected named project only after definitive absence. Recover a duplicate-create race by bounded exact relookup; auth, ambiguous lookup, transport errors, and 5xx are blockers rather than absence. When optional report resource inputs are blank, use the application loaded SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT_ID or SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT before selecting a default. If neither exists, add proposed Project name python-ai-assistant-demo to the actual loaded env/config profile, preserving existing unrelated and OTel settings. Explicit selected targets must update the effective launch profile before provisioning; no selected AO finding means no resource creation.
acceptance_criteria: The selected project identifier resolves to a real Agent Observability project; if access is unavailable, record the exact authorization blocker.

An existing selected project is reused with no create call; a definitively missing named project is created once; repeated runs and duplicate-create races converge on the same exact project ID. A missing supplied ID, ambiguous match, or failed lookup does not trigger creation.
constraints: Do not fabricate a project or identifier, and keep access tokens in operator-owned secret storage.
follow_up_actions: Confirm the resolved project exists through the selected API endpoint before configuring its runtime export.

findings.title: Resolve a dedicated Agent Stream
findings.gap: The target project has no resolved dedicated Agent Stream resource or identifier for this application.
findings.impact: The application has no verified stream destination and its traces can mix with unrelated agents.
findings.product_outcome: A dedicated Agent Stream exists in the resolved project and can be selected as the trace destination.
findings.required_fix: Resolve an existing dedicated Agent Stream resource in the selected project, or create one through the configured supported Agent Observability SDK/API endpoint when authorized; never invent an identifier or configure a global Studio stream destination. Preserve an optional operator stream name or ID and verify project ownership before binding. Reuse an exact stream within the resolved project, create only a definitively missing selected named stream, and recover a duplicate-create conflict only through bounded exact lookup in that same project. A stream in another project and failed or ambiguous lookups are explicit blockers. When optional report inputs are blank, preserve the application loaded SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM_ID or SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM. If neither exists, add proposed Agent Stream name python-ai-assistant-demo-live to the actual loaded env/config profile. Load the profile with the project runner supported env-file mechanism or an existing supported loader, not an invented dotenv parser; verify that provisioning and the real launch consume the same effective selectors.
acceptance_criteria: The selected Agent Stream identifier resolves to a real stream in the selected project; if access is unavailable, record the exact authorization blocker.

When both resources exist, neither is created. When the project exists and the selected named stream is missing, only that stream is created. When both named resources are missing, the project is created before its stream. Duplicate conflicts converge through exact relookup; mismatched stream ownership, 401/403, transport failures, and 5xx never trigger speculative creation.
constraints: Do not fabricate a stream or identifier, and keep access tokens out of tracked files.
follow_up_actions: Confirm the resolved stream belongs to the selected project before configuring per-request runtime routing.

findings.title: Persist supported Agent Observability runtime routing
findings.gap: The application deployment has no durable supported API/ingest endpoint configuration and per-request binding for its resolved project and Agent Stream.
findings.impact: Traces can remain unassigned, mix with other applications, or be mistaken for cloud Agent Observability delivery after only local or APM receipt.
findings.product_outcome: The deployed application uses ordinary supported SDK/API calls and OTLP export to its selected project and dedicated Agent Stream through the selected gateway or explicit direct-cloud endpoint.
findings.required_fix: Persist supported SDK API/console/auth configuration and the matching ingest endpoint for the installed version. Preserve explicit operator destinations and direct-cloud mode; a compatible Studio gateway is optional and its absence does not block source work or credential-free resolver tests. Keep cloud realm/token server-side in gateway mode and bind the project/Agent Stream on each request/export, without a Studio-specific application adapter, startup discovery, or global destination registration.
acceptance_criteria: Normal SDK/API resource calls and the exporter exercise the selected endpoint mode. Gateway mode derives upstream realm/auth from the active Studio connection with no application cloud token; explicit direct-cloud mode remains valid.

Two application streams preserve distinct project/stream bindings per request without cross-application leakage or changing a global AO destination. Unavailable or changed gateway connections are reported without silent destination switches or reuse of old-organization IDs.

A fresh application trace is visible in the selected cloud Agent Stream. Local receipt, resource API success, upstream ingest acknowledgement, or ordinary APM visibility alone leaves cloud AO delivery Not proven.
Configured endpoints and project/Agent Stream identifiers remain operator-overridable; cloud secrets are not committed and gateway local credentials are not represented as cloud credentials.

Blank optional resource fields use existing app env selectors or audit-disclosed stable defaults in the real loaded profile. Explicit selected targets update that effective profile before resource resolution; unrelated settings and OTel configuration remain intact. A safe example profile alone is insufficient if the launch never loads the actual settings.
constraints: Use only supported normal SDK configuration and documented routing headers or attributes; preserve selected operator endpoints and managed dependencies/lockfiles.

Do not patch SDK vendors, mix incompatible endpoint and realm modes, discover Studio endpoints at app startup, or introduce an application-specific gateway API. A selected gateway is an honest runtime availability dependency.
follow_up_actions: Exercise ordinary resource calls and fresh trace export using the configured endpoint mode, then confirm the exact fresh interaction in its intended cloud project and Agent Stream. Keep configuration, gateway receipt/forwarding, and cloud visibility evidence separate.

scenarios.trigger: Execute the selected live application resource resolver through fake supported SDK/network boundaries for both existing, both missing, existing project with missing stream, explicit IDs, repeated runs, duplicate-create races, ambiguous identities, mismatched stream ownership, and lookup/create auth or outage failures
scenarios.expected_signals: Exact project and project-scoped stream lookups, minimal ordered create calls for conclusively missing named resources, bounded conflict relookup, verified resource IDs, and continued independent application OpenTelemetry behavior when AO resource setup is blocked
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: Assertions execute the actual application resolver and inspect call order/counts, ID and ownership binding, and repeated-run state. Both-existing has zero creates; both-missing creates one project then one stream; mixed state creates only the missing stream. Races relookup the exact identity and converge; supplied IDs are never recreated; wrong ownership, ambiguity, 401/403, transport errors, and 5xx do not become absence. Report fake configuration proof separately from actual resource reuse/creation attempts and fresh cloud Agent Stream receipt; a failed AO setup leaves unrelated OTel usable without a half-bound AO sink.
